title: A literal item replaced by a sequence holding the same keep literal as the next item keeps the keep chomping
notes:
Item 1 is a keep literal `|+`; the patch replaces it with a sequence of one string, `"tail

"`, which is exactly what every later item already holds (`- - |+` over `tail` and one empty line). A string that ends in two line breaks reads back exactly only when the literal has the keep indicator: with clip (`|`) the scalar is `tail
`, with strip it is `tail` (productions 164 to 168). The new text is the old node's style, a literal, inside a block sequence written in the compact form, with the content indentation of the sibling items; the kit has no convention that fixes the style of a string inside a collection that replaces a scalar, but the old style and the siblings agree, so that is what the case states, and it is a kit convention (docs/edit-semantics.md). Only bytes of item 1 change. The input is over 512 bytes because a library may edit by region above a size threshold, a different path from the one small documents take.

provenance.reference: A writer that, for a value equal to the next item, copied the next item's text but dropped its keep indicator, so the value read back as `tail` with one line break.
